1	# Shared Technical Standards
2	
3	Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
8	
9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
10	
11	| Banned Feature | Description |
12	|----------------|-------------|
13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
14	| `mask` | Masks |
15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
30	
31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
32	|---------------|---------------------|
33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
37	
38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference
43	
44	### Presentations
45	
46	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
47	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
48	| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
49	| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |
50	
51	### Social Media
52	
53	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
54	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
55	| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
56	| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
57	| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
58	
59	### Marketing Materials
60	
61	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
62	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
63	| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
64	| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
65	| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
66	| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
71	
72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
84	
85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
86	
87	```bash
88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
90	
91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
93	
94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
97	```
98	
99	**Prohibited**:
100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
103	
104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
109	
110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
111	
112	### Shadow
113	
114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
115	
116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
117	
118	```xml
119	<defs>
120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
125	    <feMerge>
126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
128	    </feMerge>
129	  </filter>
130	</defs>
131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
132	```
133	
134	Recommended parameters:
135	```
136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
139	dx:             0–2
140	```
141	
142	#### Colored Shadow
143	
144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
145	
146	```xml
147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
152	  <feMerge>
153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
155	  </feMerge>
156	</filter>
157	```
158	
159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
160	
161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
162	
163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
164	
165	```xml
166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
170	<!-- Main card -->
171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
172	```
173	
174	### Image Overlay
175	
176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
177	
178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
187	  </linearGradient>
188	</defs>
189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
190	```
191	
192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
195	
196	```xml
197	<defs>
198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```
205	
206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
207	
208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
209	
210	```xml
211	<defs>
212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
215	  </radialGradient>
216	</defs>
217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
218	```
219	
220	#### Brand Color Overlay
221	
222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
223	
224	```xml
225	<defs>
226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
229	  </linearGradient>
230	</defs>
231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
232	```
233	
234	### Quick-Reference Table
235	
236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 7. Project Directory Structure
248	
249	```
250	project/
251	├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
252	├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
253	├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
254	├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
255	│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
256	├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
257	└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
258	```
259

But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.

# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

### Quick-Reference Table

| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

---

## 7. Project Directory Structure

```
project/
├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
```

# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

### Quick-Reference Table

| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

---

## 7. Project Directory Structure

```
project/
├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
```

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="headerGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#0D47A1"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1565C0"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <filter id="cardShadow" x="-10%" y="-10%" width="130%" height="130%">
      <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6"/>
      <feOffset dx="0" dy="3" result="offsetBlur"/>
      <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
      <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
      <feMerge>
        <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
        <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
      </feMerge>
    </filter>
  </defs>

  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="8" fill="url(#headerGrad)"/>

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="60" y="60" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#0D47A1">
    <tspan>The LLM Scaling Dilemma: Performance vs. Cost & Speed</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="60" y="80" width="1160" height="44" rx="6" fill="#1565C0" fill-opacity="0.06"/>
  <text x="80" y="108" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>Larger models improve quality, but conventional scaling hits a wall on training cost, KV cache, and throughput.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Problem statement - left side -->
  <text x="60" y="175" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>The Core Problem</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="210" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>Scaling dense Transformer LLMs yields better intelligence,</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="233" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>but at exponentially higher training and inference costs.</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="268" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>Multi-Head Attention (MHA) caches full K, V per head per</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="291" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>token, creating massive KV cache bottlenecks at scale.</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="326" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>Existing alternatives (GQA, MQA) reduce cache but</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="349" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>sacrifice model quality — a suboptimal trade-off.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Arrow pointing to solution -->
  <text x="60" y="400" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">
    <tspan>What's needed: efficiency without performance loss</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Three pain-point cards on the right -->
  <!-- Card 1: Training Cost -->
  <rect x="680" y="155" width="260" height="155" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="680" y="155" width="260" height="6" rx="3" fill="#C62828"/>
  <use data-icon="rocket" x="700" y="180" width="32" height="32" fill="#C62828"/>
  <text x="740" y="204" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>Training Cost</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="700" y="235" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>Dense models require massive</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="700" y="255" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>compute; all parameters activated</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="700" y="275" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>for every single token.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Card 2: KV Cache -->
  <rect x="960" y="155" width="260" height="155" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="960" y="155" width="260" height="6" rx="3" fill="#E65100"/>
  <use data-icon="database" x="980" y="180" width="32" height="32" fill="#E65100"/>
  <text x="1020" y="204" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>KV Cache Bottleneck</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="980" y="235" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>MHA stores full K, V per head</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="980" y="255" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>per token — memory grows</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="980" y="275" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>linearly with sequence length.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Card 3: Throughput -->
  <rect x="680" y="335" width="260" height="155" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="680" y="335" width="260" height="6" rx="3" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <use data-icon="bolt" x="700" y="360" width="32" height="32" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <text x="740" y="384" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>Generation Throughput</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="700" y="415" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>Large KV caches and dense</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="700" y="435" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>computation limit tokens/sec</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="700" y="455" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>during autoregressive decoding.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Solution card -->
  <rect x="960" y="335" width="260" height="155" rx="10" fill="#1565C0" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="#1565C0" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="1090" y="385" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0" text-anchor="middle">
    <tspan>DeepSeek-V2 Solution</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="980" y="415" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>MLA: compress KV cache</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="980" y="435" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>DeepSeekMoE: sparse FFN</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="980" y="460" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">
    <tspan>= Strong + Economical + Fast</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="60" y1="660" x2="1220" y2="660" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="1220" y="690" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#95A5A6" text-anchor="end">
    <tspan>DeepSeek-V2  |  2</tspan>
  </text>
</svg>

  </text>

  </text>

  </text>
  <text x="60" y="295" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">

  </text>
  <text x="60" y="320" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">

  </text>

    <tspan>60 Transformer layers</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="60" y1="660" x2="1220" y2="660" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="60" y="690" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#95A5A6">

  <!-- LLaMA 3 70B: 70B, 77.0 -->
  <circle cx="841" cy="271" r="9" fill="#78909C" filter="url(#dotShadow)"/>

  <line x1="1000" y1="198" x2="1220" y2="198" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1"/>

  <text x="1000" y="225" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>DeepSeek-V2 achieves the</tspan>

  <text x="1000" y="245" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">
    <tspan>highest MMLU (78.5)</tspan>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="headerGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#0D47A1"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1565C0"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <filter id="cardShadow" x="-10%" y="-10%" width="130%" height="130%">
      <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6"/>
      <feOffset dx="0" dy="3" result="offsetBlur"/>
      <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
      <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
      <feMerge>
        <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
        <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
      </feMerge>
    </filter>
  </defs>

  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="8" fill="url(#headerGrad)"/>

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="60" y="60" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" fill="#0D47A1">
    <tspan>Chat (RL) Rivals Closed-Source Models on Chinese Benchmarks</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Takeaway box -->
  <rect x="60" y="80" width="1160" height="44" rx="6" fill="#1565C0" fill-opacity="0.06"/>
  <text x="80" y="108" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>After SFT + GRPO-based RL, DeepSeek-V2 Chat outperforms all open-source and most closed-source models in Chinese.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Left side: Alignment Pipeline -->
  <text x="60" y="170" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>Alignment Pipeline</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Step 1: SFT -->
  <rect x="60" y="195" width="480" height="75" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#1565C0" stroke-width="1.5" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="195" width="8" height="75" rx="4" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <text x="85" y="222" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">
    <tspan>Step 1: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="85" y="250" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>1.5 million conversational sessions</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Arrow -->
  <line x1="300" y1="270" x2="300" y2="295" stroke="#5D6D7E" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="300,302 294,292 306,292" fill="#5D6D7E"/>

  <!-- Step 2: RL -->
  <rect x="60" y="305" width="480" height="75" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2E7D32" stroke-width="1.5" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="305" width="8" height="75" rx="4" fill="#2E7D32"/>
  <text x="85" y="332" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2E7D32">
    <tspan>Step 2: Reinforcement Learning (GRPO)</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="85" y="360" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>Group Relative Policy Optimization — no critic model needed</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Arrow -->
  <line x1="300" y1="380" x2="300" y2="405" stroke="#5D6D7E" stroke-width="2"/>
  <polygon points="300,412 294,402 306,402" fill="#5D6D7E"/>

  <!-- Result -->
  <rect x="60" y="415" width="480" height="50" rx="10" fill="#0D47A1" fill-opacity="0.08" stroke="#1565C0" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="300" y="447" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#0D47A1" text-anchor="middle">
    <tspan>DeepSeek-V2 Chat (RL)</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Right side: Benchmark Results -->
  <text x="610" y="170" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>Chat Evaluation Results</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Metric Card 1: AlpacaEval -->
  <rect x="610" y="195" width="310" height="125" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="626" y="215" width="6" height="50" rx="3" fill="#1565C0"/>
  <text x="648" y="237" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>AlpacaEval 2.0</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="648" y="255" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#95A5A6">
    <tspan>Length-controlled win rate</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="648" y="300" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1565C0">
    <tspan>38.9%</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Metric Card 2: MT-Bench -->
  <rect x="940" y="195" width="280" height="125" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="956" y="215" width="6" height="50" rx="3" fill="#2E7D32"/>
  <text x="978" y="237" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>MT-Bench</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="978" y="255" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#95A5A6">
    <tspan>Overall score</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="978" y="300" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#2E7D32">
    <tspan>8.97</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Metric Card 3: AlignBench (highlighted) -->
  <rect x="610" y="340" width="610" height="135" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#1565C0" stroke-width="2" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="626" y="360" width="6" height="50" rx="3" fill="#E65100"/>
  <text x="648" y="382" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>AlignBench (Chinese)</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="648" y="400" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#95A5A6">
    <tspan>Overall score</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="648" y="448" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#E65100">
    <tspan>7.91</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Highlight badge -->
  <rect x="830" y="370" width="370" height="80" rx="8" fill="#E65100" fill-opacity="0.06"/>
  <use data-icon="star" x="845" y="385" width="24" height="24" fill="#E65100"/>
  <text x="878" y="402" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#E65100">
    <tspan>Best-in-Class (Chinese)</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="845" y="428" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>Outperforms all open-source models</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="845" y="446" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#5D6D7E">
    <tspan>and most closed-source models</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Bottom note -->
  <rect x="60" y="510" width="1160" height="110" rx="10" fill="#F5F7FA" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="80" y="540" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>What Makes GRPO Different?</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="80" y="568" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">

  </text>

  <rect x="60" y="150" width="1160" height="85" rx="10" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E0E0E0" stroke-width="1" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="150" width="8" height="85" rx="4" fill="#1565C0"/>

    <tspan>1</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="132" y="183" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">
    <tspan>MLA is a strictly better alternative to GQA/MQA for inference efficiency</tspan>
  </text>

  </text>

  </text>

  </text>
  <text x="132" y="310" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">

    <tspan>4</tspan>
  </text>
  <text x="132" y="483" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#2C3E50">

  </text>
  <text x="132" y="510" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#5D6D7E">

  </text>

arguments.content:
# 01_title_slide

Welcome everyone. Today I'm presenting DeepSeek-V2, a Mixture-of-Experts language model that achieves a remarkable balance between performance and efficiency. [Pause]

The model has 236 billion total parameters but activates only 21 billion per token, supports 128K context length, and was pretrained on 8.1 trillion tokens. These numbers set the stage for what we'll explore today — how architectural innovation can break the scaling-cost trade-off.

Key points: (1) 236B total / 21B activated MoE architecture (2) Two core innovations: MLA and DeepSeekMoE (3) Achieves top-tier performance at a fraction of the cost
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_motivation

[Transition] Before diving into the architecture, let's understand the problem DeepSeek-V2 is solving.

The fundamental dilemma in LLM scaling is straightforward: bigger models perform better, but they cost exponentially more to train and serve. [Data] A 70B dense model activates all 70 billion parameters for every single token — that's an enormous compute burden. [Pause]

The KV cache problem is equally severe. Standard Multi-Head Attention stores full key and value vectors per head per token. As sequence length grows, memory consumption becomes the primary bottleneck for generation throughput. Existing alternatives like GQA and MQA trade quality for cache reduction — a suboptimal compromise. DeepSeek-V2 asks: can we have both?

Key points: (1) Dense scaling hits cost and memory walls (2) KV cache is the primary inference bottleneck (3) GQA/MQA sacrifice quality for efficiency
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_architecture_overview

[Transition] DeepSeek-V2 answers that question with two complementary architectural innovations.

At a high level, each of the 60 Transformer blocks replaces the standard attention mechanism with Multi-Head Latent Attention, or MLA, and replaces the dense feed-forward network with DeepSeekMoE. [Pause]

MLA handles the attention efficiency problem — compressing the KV cache by over 93%. DeepSeekMoE handles the compute efficiency problem — activating only 21 billion of the 236 billion parameters per token. The model was pretrained on 8.1 trillion tokens from a multi-source corpus with extended Chinese data, and supports a 128K token context window.

Key points: (1) MLA replaces MHA for cache efficiency (2) DeepSeekMoE replaces dense FFN for compute efficiency (3) 236B total, 21B activated, 128K context
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 04_mla_mechanism

[Transition] Let's look at MLA in detail — this is the key innovation for inference efficiency.

The comparison here shows four attention mechanisms side by side. Standard MHA caches full K and V vectors for every head — that's 100% cache usage and the best quality, but the worst memory footprint. GQA shares KV across groups, roughly halving the cache. MQA goes further with a single shared KV, but at significant quality cost. [Pause]

[Data] MLA takes a completely different approach. Instead of reducing heads, it compresses the full K and V into a compact latent vector — only 6.7% of the original cache size, a 93.3% reduction. The key insight is that full keys and values are then reconstructed on-the-fly through learned projection matrices. A decoupled RoPE component handles positional encoding separately. The result? Better performance than MHA with dramatically less cache.

Key points: (1) Low-rank KV joint compression to latent vectors (2) On-the-fly reconstruction preserves quality (3) 93.3% cache reduction while exceeding MHA performance
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_deepseek_moe

[Transition] Now let's examine the compute side — the DeepSeekMoE architecture.

The FFN layers use a mixture of two expert types. Shared experts are always activated for every token — they capture common knowledge that all inputs need. Routed experts are sparsely activated through a top-K router, where each token is sent to only a small subset of specialists. [Pause]

Three design choices make this work at scale. First, fine-grained expert segmentation — using more, smaller experts increases specialization. Second, device-limited routing constrains each token to experts on at most M devices, dramatically reducing cross-node communication. Third, auxiliary losses ensure balanced expert utilization, and a token-dropping strategy during training prevents overflow without affecting inference.

Key points: (1) Shared experts for common knowledge, routed for specialization (2) Device-limited routing reduces communication overhead (3) Auxiliary losses maintain load balance
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_efficiency_gains

[Transition] So what do these architectural innovations actually deliver in practice? Let's look at the numbers.

Compared to DeepSeek 67B — the dense predecessor — the gains are dramatic across all three dimensions. [Data] Training cost drops by 42.5%, because the MoE architecture activates only 21 billion of 236 billion parameters per token. [Data] KV cache shrinks by 93.3%, thanks to MLA's latent compression. And generation throughput improves by 5.76 times, combining both the reduced memory footprint and sparse computation. [Pause]

These aren't incremental improvements — they represent a fundamental shift in the cost-performance curve. The MLA and DeepSeekMoE innovations are complementary: one handles attention efficiency, the other handles compute efficiency.

Key points: (1) 42.5% lower training cost from MoE sparsity (2) 93.3% KV cache reduction from MLA (3) 5.76× throughput from combined innovations
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 07_mmlu_performance

[Transition] Efficiency gains only matter if performance holds up. Let's examine the MMLU benchmark results.

This scatter plot is the key chart of the presentation. The x-axis shows activated parameters, the y-axis shows MMLU score. [Pause] DeepSeek-V2 sits in the upper-left corner — the Pareto-optimal position. [Data] With only 21 billion activated parameters, it scores 78.5 on MMLU, surpassing LLaMA 3 70B at 77.0, Mixtral 8×22B at 77.6, and Qwen1.5 72B at 75.6. That's roughly 3.3 times fewer activated parameters than LLaMA 3 70B, yet 1.5 points higher on the benchmark. [Pause]

This is the clearest evidence that DeepSeek-V2 breaks the traditional scaling curve. You don't need to activate 70 billion parameters to achieve 70B-class performance.

Key points: (1) MMLU 78.5 — highest among open-source models (2) 21B activated params — 3.3× fewer than LLaMA 3 70B (3) Pareto-optimal: best performance per activated parameter
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_alignment_results

[Transition] Beyond base model performance, let's look at how DeepSeek-V2 performs after alignment.

The alignment pipeline has two stages. First, supervised fine-tuning on 1.5 million conversational sessions. Then, reinforcement learning using GRPO — Group Relative Policy Optimization — which estimates baselines from group scores, eliminating the need for a separate critic model. [Pause]

The results are strong across the board. [Data] On AlpacaEval 2.0, it achieves a 38.9% length-controlled win rate. MT-Bench overall score is 8.97. And on AlignBench for Chinese, it scores 7.91 — outperforming all open-source models and most closed-source models. This makes DeepSeek-V2 Chat the strongest open-source Chinese chat model available.

Key points: (1) SFT on 1.5M sessions + GRPO-based RL (2) Best-in-class Chinese performance (AlignBench 7.91) (3) Competitive with closed-source systems in English
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 09_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five key takeaways from this work.

First, MLA is a strictly better alternative to GQA and MQA — it reduces KV cache by 93.3% while actually improving over MHA performance. Second, DeepSeekMoE with fine-grained experts enables training a 236B model at 42.5% lower cost than a 67B dense model. [Pause]

Third, only 21B activated parameters are needed to match or exceed 70B-class dense models on MMLU. Fourth, the 5.76× throughput improvement makes DeepSeek-V2 practical for real-world deployment at scale. And fifth, after alignment, it's the strongest open-source Chinese chat model while remaining competitive in English.

The overarching message: architectural innovation — not brute-force scaling — is the path to efficient, powerful language models. [Pause] Thank you.

Key points: (1) MLA > MHA with 93.3% less cache (2) MoE: 236B at 42.5% less cost (3) 21B params beat 70B dense (4) 5.76× throughput (5) Best open-source Chinese chat
Duration: 1.5 minutes

The KV cache problem is equally severe. Standard Multi-Head Attention stores full key and value vectors per head per token. [Transition] Let's look at MLA in detail — this is the key innovation for inference efficiency.

The comparison here shows four attention mechanisms side by side. Standard MHA caches full K and V vectors for every head — that's 100% cache usage and the best quality, but the worst memory footprint. GQA shares KV across groups, roughly halving the cache. MQA goes further with a single shared KV, but at significant quality cost. [Pause]

steps.message:
The presentation has been saved to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx` (80KB, 9 slides with speaker notes).

**Summary of the deck:**
1. **Title Slide** — Model name, key stats (236B/21B/128K), paper attribution
2. **Motivation** — LLM scaling dilemma with three pain-point cards
3. **Architecture Overview** — Transformer block diagram showing MLA + DeepSeekMoE
4. **MLA Mechanism** — Four-column comparison (MHA/GQA/MQA/MLA) with cache reduction visualization
